paper_title: What are they talking about Benchmarking Large Language Models for   Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization
caption: Paragraph retrieval ratios 0.90\% of LLMs. The majority of LLMs can be classified as either conservative (ratio<300.90{%}) or open retrievers (ratio>380.90{%}).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the paragraph retrieval ratios (expressed as percentages) for a set of large language models (LLMs) evaluated in the context of knowledge-grounded discussion summarization. The horizontal axis lists the LLMs in a left-to-right order: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Max, and GLM-4-Plus. The vertical axis represents the retrieval ratio in percentage, ranging from 0 to 50 with linear increments of 10. Each model is represented by a single colored bar, with values explicitly labeled on top of each bar. The retrieval ratios vary across models: GPT-4o has 34.11%, GPT-4o-mini 29.07%, Claude 3 Opus 29.16%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 25.92%, Gemini 1.5 Pro 31.56%, Llama-3.1-405B 28.49%, Mistral Large 39.37%, DeepSeek-V3 37.99%, Qwen-Max 46.94%, and GLM-4-Plus 43.58%. The bars are arranged in the order of the models as listed, not sorted by value. The model with the highest retrieval ratio is Qwen-Max (46.94%), followed by GLM-4-Plus (43.58%) and Mistral Large (39.37%). The lowest retrieval ratio is observed in Claude 3.5 Sonnet (25.92%), followed by Gemini 1.5 Pro (31.56%) and Llama-3.1-405B (28.49%). The chart includes a red label “Expert” near the top-left corner, possibly indicating a benchmark or reference point, though it is not directly tied to any bar. The caption notes that 0.90% of LLMs are considered, and that most models fall into either conservative (ratio < 30.90%) or open retriever (ratio > 38.09%) categories, though the exact threshold values in the caption appear to contain typographical errors (e.g., “300.90{%}” likely intended as “30.90%”).
